title: A sandbox for scripts
description:
A program that runs scripts written by its users must decide what those scripts may touch, just as a C program embedding Lua opens only the libraries it wants. Do the same from Lua with `load` and an environment table.

```lua-norun
make_env()                -- a NEW table with only these: print, pairs, ipairs, tostring, tonumber, type, select,
                          -- error, pcall, and the libraries string, table and math. No os, io, load, require, debug,
                          -- setmetatable or _G.
run_script(code, env)     -- compiles code as text only (never binary chunks) with env as its globals, under the name
                          -- "script", and runs it. Returns true and the script's first result, or false and the
                          -- error message, both for errors while compiling and while running.
```

Changes a script makes to its globals land in `env`, never in your program's own globals.

```lua-norun
run_script("return 6 * 7", make_env())       --> true, 42
run_script("os.exit(1)", make_env())         --> false, "[string "script"]:1: attempt to index a nil value (global 'os')"
```
hints: `load(code, name, mode, env)`: mode `"t"` accepts only text, and `env` becomes the chunk's globals. It returns `nil` and a message when the code does not compile.
Run the compiled function with `pcall`, so an error in the script comes back as `false` and the message.
unitTests:
test("the environment has only the safe parts", function()
    local env = make_env()
    for _, name in ipairs({ "print", "pairs", "ipairs", "tostring", "tonumber", "type", "select", "error", "pcall", "string", "table", "math" }) do
        check(env[name] == _G[name], name .. " should be there")
    end
    for _, name in ipairs({ "os", "io", "load", "require", "debug", "setmetatable", "_G", "dofile", "loadfile" }) do
        check(env[name] == nil, name .. " must not be there")
    end
    check(make_env() ~= make_env(), "each call makes a new table")
end)

test("scripts can compute", function()
    check_eq({ run_script("return 6 * 7", make_env()) }, { true, 42 })
    check_eq({ run_script("local t = {} for i = 1, 3 do t[i] = i * i end return table.concat(t, ',')", make_env()) }, { true, "1,4,9" })
    check_eq({ run_script("x = 1", make_env()) }, { true, nil })
end)

test("scripts cannot reach os or io", function()
    local ok, err = run_script("os.exit(1)", make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
    check(tostring(err):find("os") ~= nil, "the error mentions os")
    ok = run_script("io.open('secret.txt', 'w')", make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
    ok = run_script("return require('os')", make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
end)

test("script globals stay in the environment", function()
    local env = make_env()
    run_script("score = 100 function bonus() return score * 2 end", env)
    check_eq(env.score, 100)
    check_eq(rawget(_G, "score"), nil, "the script's global leaked into the program")
    check_eq({ run_script("return bonus()", env) }, { true, 200 })
end)

test("errors are reported, not raised", function()
    local ok, err = run_script("return 1 +", make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
    check(tostring(err):find("script") ~= nil, "a syntax error names the script")
    ok, err = run_script("error('custom failure')", make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
    check(tostring(err):find("custom failure", 1, true) ~= nil, "a run-time error keeps its message")
end)

test("binary chunks are refused", function()
    local binary = string.dump(function() return 1 end)
    local ok = run_script(binary, make_env())
    check_eq(ok, false)
end)
